rounds.notes:
When playing Stadium as Tracer, there are three truths: building a strong econ wins games, you can’t farm Stadium Cash if you’re dead, and you die very easily. With that in mind, we’re going to play with the mindset of a gnat - but a ***smart gnat***. Your starting items will make you just enough of a threat to force enemies to turn around, but unless you’re going in with full cooldowns or taking a 1v1 against someone already half health, there’s a good chance you die. And **we do not want to die**. Play safe, harass the backline, and chip away at their mental. You’ll hit a power spike in round 3 that upgrades you from gnat to mosquito, but until then, patience is key.

For the first power, we pick [T.Racer](item_996e13d5-9521-4312-944f-d672f528776b) because we’re here to play mind games. Beyond the obvious benefit of extra blink distance, you’ll be surprised how much harder this makes you to track - especially for experienced Overwatch players. Muscle memory betrays enemy hitscans who expect you to appear 3 meters closer than you actually do, and that adjustment is harder than you’d think. It will take some getting used to on your end too, but the third-person perspective helps a lot with learning the new blink spacing. Picking this power first ensures you’ll have plenty of time to acclimate. At worst, spend a bit of time in the Stadium practice range. Sure, you’ll run into a handful of Cassidys or Soldiers who figure it out and swap into auto-targeting builds, but by the time they do, you should already have the survivability to deal with it.

For starting items, the only potential swap is trading [First Aid Kit](item_0172eaaa-1902-44a3-b989-d12f0f7301da) for [Ballistic Buffer](item_40146dd3-a8cb-40ca-8917-c430bfa2be0e) if you’re facing hitscans who poke you down. Otherwise, turn their backline into your frontline, pressure the supports, always save a blink to get out, and farm away.

round_upgrades.notes: Use this if you are worried about getting poked down from a distance (Ash/Soldier/Cassidy/Freja)

rounds.notes:
Round 2:

This round we start to build up our survivability. Typically we are up against weapon damage so I pick up [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09), but alternatively, if you notice they are building mostly ability power swap this out for [Reinforced Titanium](item_8ebaa7db-aedf-48ed-adc1-318cb46a3214).

If the enemy team has a mix of heroes building ability and weapon power, buy both. The main goal here is to farm cash and the most consistent way to do that is staying alive.

After our survivability item(s) we prioritize attack speed with [Aftermarket Firing Pin](item_2485b212-b286-42d0-a2bd-20eb4396b054). Use any excess stadium cash on the items below (prioritize top to bottom based on what you can afford).

•	[Talon Modification Module](item_c0ca1795-a3ea-4dc9-ae17-f34122574b3a)

•	[Compensator](item_2a354f80-610c-4661-9bdd-8960ae1a60b0)

•	[Weapon Grease](item_961ae72f-434f-406b-a89b-ab8efec806bf)

•	[Ammo Reserves](item_982d53aa-5ef4-493f-93e7-9e374d0ebf34)

round_upgrades.notes: Swap this out for Reinforced Titanium if the enemy team is mostly ability power.

Pick this up *in lieu* of Crusader Hydraulics if the enemy team is building mostly ability power. 

Pick this up *with* Crusader Hydraulics if the enemy team has a mix of ability and weapon damage builds.
Use this if you are worried about getting poked down from a distance (Ash/Soldier/Cassidy/Freja)

rounds.notes:
Alright, we’ve now hit *mosquito*. Looking at our second power, we technically have two paths forward depending on how the first two rounds have gone. If you’ve been playing like a smart gnat and finding success, congrats - we’re taking [Foresight](item_f4163ce1-8f80-43ca-85d4-39812084400f) to upgrade our backline harassment from a tickle to a sting.

If you’ve been playing like a *smart gnat* but keep dying to burst damage (which should be the only thing killing you if you’re playing correctly), then we take [Auto Recall](item_ae3dbebf-c306-4408-b698-6f666ace0a7c) first.

If you haven’t been playing like a *smart gnat*… come on, man. We talked about this. Remember: living = strong econ, strong econ = win. We want to win (in case I hadn’t covered that already). Drink some water, sit up straight, lock in, and let’s get back on track, champ. ***forehead kiss***

Regardless of the power you take, the item priority stays the same: [Overdrive Core](item_a2a8dba1-5f2f-4da1-9445-b08f49162121). If you can’t afford it, the path splits based on your power choice. Buy items top to bottom by tier (if you can’t afford more blue, move on to the first green).

***Got Foresight but can’t afford Overdrive Core:***

[Talon Modification Module](item_c0ca1795-a3ea-4dc9-ae17-f34122574b3a)

[Pulse Detector](item_79ddef46-8917-4d8f-a123-7ddb589ad3e7) (if you can’t afford Talon Modification Module)

[Reinforced Titanium](item_8ebaa7db-aedf-48ed-adc1-318cb46a3214)

[Vishkar Condensor](item_086a91da-b65d-4047-8fc7-28a992078b1d) (if you already have Reinforced Titanium)

[First Aid Kit](item_0172eaaa-1902-44a3-b989-d12f0f7301da)

***Got Auto Recall but can’t afford Overdrive Core:***

[Reinforced Titanium](item_8ebaa7db-aedf-48ed-adc1-318cb46a3214) (if you already have Crusader Hydraulics)

[Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09) (if you already have Reinforced Titanium)

[Vishkar Condensor](item_086a91da-b65d-4047-8fc7-28a992078b1d)

[Vital-E-Tee](item_b92e6f1d-3aac-4eec-b027-00c8e1529016)

[First Aid Kit](item_0172eaaa-1902-44a3-b989-d12f0f7301da)

In the optional items, you’ll start seeing situational picks I’ve swapped in from time to time depending on the match, as well as options for when you’ve got excess Stadium Cash (yay!). Check the notes on each item to see what I’d replace it with, and make adjustments as needed. For situational swaps, trust your gut and keep the core goal in mind: always stay alive. If you’re alive, you’re drawing attention, farming cash, driving supports crazy - in short, you’re bringing value to the team.

rounds.notes:
So… we didn’t mercy rule them this game. Well, that’s too bad for them - now we get to start having some real fun. Let’s scoop up [Booster Jets](item_a291de85-b6d9-43cf-b5da-f3184a156f48) (but if you missed [Overdrive Core](item_a2a8dba1-5f2f-4da1-9445-b08f49162121) last round, grab that first). Sell what you need to in order to get the three items marked with the gold “important” star. From here on out, that’s the mindset: sell whatever you need to, because those core starred items are non-negotiable. Hopefully this round you can hang onto Aftermarket Firing Pin and Ammo Reserves, but if not, fill in the open slots with green items, prioritizing in this order: 

Attack Speed > Ammo > Weapon Power.

And don’t forget - keep those optional items and their notes in mind as you go. They can make the difference depending on the match.

round_upgrades.notes: Still playing "walking to point from spawn" simulator? Take this for another get-out-of-jail free card.

Buy if you have an excess of Stadium Cash burning a hole in your pocket (or you can feasibly keep the starred "important items" listed above, sell the rest, and take this instead if you find you need more weapon power.
Swap this out for Reinforced Titanium if the enemy team is mostly ability power.

rounds.notes:
Round five is where this build comes fully online. For your third power, pick up whichever option you didn’t take in round three.

Now you:

Move faster

Blink further

Have legal aim-bot for 2 seconds on landing

Carry two get-out-of-jail-free cards between Auto Recall and the 300 overhealth from Overdrive Core

This is where we go from mosquito to wasp.

For items, we’re grabbing [Vanadium Injection](item_57953fbc-11ff-4e92-9928-fc59b7be668f). Which means: no more ult. I know, I know… tragic. But here’s the thing - we all want to be Kabaji, but let’s be realistic. The cooldown reduction, bonus health, attack speed, and weapon power are far more consistent than landing a Pulse Bomb. Do not use Pulse Bomb. Please. (thank you).

After that, hold onto your blue survival item (typically [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09), though you may have swapped it for [Reinforced Titanium](item_8ebaa7db-aedf-48ed-adc1-318cb46a3214) if you’re against strong ability power). Beyond that, the items are flexible - build for the match you’re in. If you’re struggling to decide, or the optional items don’t fit, fall back to the simple rule: Attack Speed > Ammo > Weapon Power.

round_upgrades.notes: Swap this out for Reinforced Titanium if the enemy team is mostly ability power.

rounds.notes:
We’re still here? Well, it can’t be you (that wouldn’t be a very DPS mindset), so I can’t believe your:

a.) Tank
b.) Other DPS
c.) Support
d.) Internet Service Provider

…is throwing this hard. Don’t crash out (yet) - we can still pull this off. We ***are*** the cavalry, after all.

We’re already strong, but let’s throw one more item onto the gold-star list: [Underworld Quickloader](item_dc8e93b1-a561-4007-bfdc-42839f612d01).

With this in your inventory, you can finally part ways with [Aftermarket Firing Pin](item_2485b212-b286-42d0-a2bd-20eb4396b054) (rest in peace, king). Quickloader helps patch the ammo reserve issue you’re definitely feeling by heavily boosting reload speed just for playing the way you already are. At this stage, it also adds much-needed weapon power to the build.

If you can’t afford Quickloader without selling one of the other starred items, fill the slot with one of the optional items or any weapon-power pick ([Codebreaker](item_caa96c7e-655f-4d03-9bd9-0f41937fec27) is always solid, even if the enemy team doesn’t have much armor). 

Late game, it’s tougher to build strictly by the book - ***rounds 6 and 7 are where boys become men, girls become women, and they’s become them’s.*** Paying attention to enemy builds is the difference between dragging your team kicking and screaming to a Victory screen, or staring at that Defeat screen, reflecting on the choices that landed you here instead of just queueing Mystery Heroes.

Anything post–round 5 is fair game for tweaking with this build. I promise I won’t be *that* mad. All you need right now are deep breaths, happy thoughts, and some murderous intent.

Go get ’em, champ.

round_upgrades.notes: Swap this out for Reinforced Titanium if the enemy team is mostly ability power.

rounds.notes:
Round seven. Wow, Look at us. **Hey**, look at us. Who would’ve thought? (*not me*)

I don’t know how this game has gone. I don’t know what in your life has led you here. I don’t know what possessed you to pick up the pulse pistols and never look back. But I do know this: this is your “Miracle on Ice” moment - except not on ice, not necessarily a miracle... honestly more of an intentional harassment campaign on pavement. You get the idea. Let’s finish this. 

We’re capping this baby off with [Timelapse](item_20d43db5-d2ad-47e9-b32f-82d8eca006ce). Just in case you weren’t already ruining someone’s day, this will push them right over the edge. By now you should be nearly unkillable, and with Timelapse and your round seven item ([Commander's Clip](item_ff7cad01-2065-4908-a2c1-3bdf1458c7a4)) you’ll be unkillable and, fun fact, technically in violation of Additional Protocol I, Article 51 of the Geneva Conventions. All that to say, if your god complex hasn’t kicked in yet, don’t worry – it’s about to. 

The playstyle doesn’t change: don’t frontline unless it’s absolutely necessary, but let’s be real - if we’re in round seven, your frontliners probably aren’t front lining anyway (and it can’t be you, because that’s not a very DPS mindset). Blink, empty a clip, blink, empty a clip, blink, empty a clip, recall when low, rinse and repeat for as long as humanly possible and trust me - since at this point you’ve become less a hero and more the enemy team’s intangible sleep-paralysis demon outfitted with fully automatic mini shotguns and a British accent, it can be very long.

For additional items, I kept this build around $10,000 a round, so you’ll see a blue item listed. But realistically, you can probably afford something with more “oomph.” Use this slot for extra survivability (I’m partial to Divine Intervention) or, if you’d rather lean fully into the villain arc, grab Eye of the Spider.

Win or lose; I’m proud of you, and don’t forget the DPS creed: 

***You played perfectly. Your teammates? Bots. The enemy team? Boosted. The matchmaker? A sentient Excel sheet written on a PC running Windows Vista that knows no desire in this material world outside of ruining your SR.***

God speed.
